records.canvas_ruling: A map CANVAS CANNOT BE HONESTLY FAKED. The canvas region is therefore a TYPED ABSENCE that names WHICH absence it is: the reference's canvas draws a real basemap and its "No layers" is an EMPTY layer list on top of a map that exists; the estate's canvas is MISSING. The port renders no canvas element, no svg geometry, no tile source and no borrowed vendor basemap — a drawn map would be a fabricated reference, and it would erase exactly the missing-vs-empty distinction this program exists to hold. The four things a real canvas would need are NAMED on-surface rather than implied: a geometry-bearing record type, a coordinate reference system, a tile or vector basemap source, and a layer plane binding them — each an authority-and-plane cut, never a UI cut.

records.four_state_ruling: REFUSED is not EMPTY, EMPTY is not MISSING, and a plane with NO READ ROUTE is none of the three. A refusal is a closed door, not a measurement: rendering /v1/hypervisor/packages as "0 packages" would convert an identity-first refusal into a count the estate never took — the same defect class as reading a declared data source as extracted data (FUS-1) or drawing a plausible map (MAP-1). Every plane's state is therefore CLASSIFIED FROM ITS OWN LIVE RESPONSE ON EVERY RENDER and stamped on its row as data-ioi-plane-state, so a state can never be pasted and can never rot; a gate re-derives all ten states independently and fails on any drift.
records.authority_ruling: READ-ONLY PROJECTION. The estate's registry verbs are REAL and they are OWNED ELSEWHERE: candidate admission, release creation, release recall and uninstall belong to the closed Packages family (/__ioi/packages/registry, canonical /packages); draft → publish-candidate → review → publish belongs to Marketplace (/__ioi/marketplace/listings + the marketplace substrate lane). This landing re-mints NONE of them — the reference's "Create artifact repository" renders as a typed absence whose reason states that the verb EXISTS and names where, and the surface links there. A ported read landing never mints a second owner for a verb that already has one.

build_plane_sweep.method: probe every candidate run/build plane over the SAME identity envelope this surface renders with; keep the raw HTTP status; decide 'no read route' from the DAEMON'S OWN ROUTE INDEX (GET /v1) rather than from a status guess, because a 404 body cannot tell a missing route apart from a missing record; then classify from the response itself (a typed refusal before any collection is looked for; live-or-empty only for a 200 that actually carried a collection).
live: /v1/hypervisor/work-ledger — 7141 entries, of which 57 carry kind=run (THE build lane rendered)
/v1/hypervisor/agent-run-transcripts — 3174 run transcripts (kinds: harness-profile-op 2783 · model-route-op 301 · automation-run 50 · unkinded 40)
/v1/jobs — 10 runtime job records (jobType agent_run, status completed)
/v1/hypervisor/workruns — 4 (all open; the ONLY estate plane recording a branch + base_commit)
empty: /v1/goal-orchestration/attempts — the plane answered and holds none
/v1/hypervisor/foundry/run-plans — the plane answered and holds none
refused: /v1/hypervisor/sessions — HTTP 503 session_registry_unavailable (a recorded legacy-slot refusal, pre-existing and not this leg's)
no_read_route: /v1/hypervisor/automation-executions — the daemon's route index publishes NO route at this path at all (only /:id and /:id/cancel); HTTP 404 on GET
build_plane_sweep.verdict: the estate HAS run planes — many — so, as with the registry leg, the adjudication was never 'is there anything' but 'which plane can honestly carry a BUILD ROW'. The four states came back again and a fifth finding came with them.

union_finding.claim: NO SINGLE PLANE LISTS EVERY BUILD, and the two obvious ones each record a field the other lacks.
union_finding.why_each_projection_is_incomplete: The per-automation projection (/v1/hypervisor/automations/:id/runs) can only be reached automation by automation and the daemon publishes NO list route for automation-executions, so the 7 executions whose automation has since been deleted (auto_18bda3bafd8f31ff, auto_18bda68ea6706c5e, auto_18bda74bfd502ede, auto_18bda81093c48c0c) are unreachable through it forever. The transcript projection never recorded 7 other executions (all from 2026-06-25, belonging to automations that still exist) — and those same 7 are exactly the ledger entries whose state_root is EMPTY, because the state root lives on the transcript.
union_finding.disjoint_fields: The transcript projection carries state_root on 3174 of 3174 records and a principal on ZERO of them. The per-automation projection carries executor_identity on 50 of 50 and state_root on none. The work-ledger run entry carries BOTH (authority + state_root) on one record, plus automation_name, project_id, environment_id, counts, timestamp, finished_at, trigger_kind, step_results and timeline_ref.
union_finding.ruling: the builds table reads the work-ledger run lane, and the three counts that justify that choice (ledger total · transcript-reachable · fan-out-unreachable) are RE-DERIVED ON EVERY RENDER from the three planes themselves. A pasted '57 / 50 / 7' would rot the first time a build lands or an automation is deleted, and a gate fails on any drift.

records.link_not_duplicate_ruling: The 3174-record transcript plane is ALREADY rendered by the Monocle Build-timeline lane at /__ioi/lineage?tab=timeline (op/kind · status · started_at · state_root, newest 30, cap named). This surface LINKS it and does not re-render it: a second renderer over the same records is a second answer waiting to disagree, and one plane gets one renderer. The surface also names WHY the transcript plane is not the builds table — it records no principal on any record, and 3124 of its 3174 records are hypervisor OPERATION transcripts (harness-profile ops, model-route ops), not builds at all.
records.column_mapping_ruling: FUS-1's column refusal applies and is made explicit on-surface as a six-row mapping table. OUTPUTS binds NOTHING: an estate build record carries no output-resource field of any kind; its step_results carry per-step evidence whose shape changes with the step kind (a command's stdout excerpt, an agent turn's conversation file, a proposal's changed files), which is evidence of how a step ran and not a list of what the build produced. The estate's nearest artifact list is artifactNames on the RUNTIME JOB plane (/v1/jobs) — a different plane holding a different noun, and no estate record joins a runtime job to a build; inventing that edge would be a fabricated column. ACTIONS binds nothing either, by DESIGN: the verbs are real (POST /v1/hypervisor/automations/:id/runs to start, POST /v1/hypervisor/automation-executions/:id/cancel to cancel) and owned by Automations, so the column carries the record's PROOF (state_root + timeline_ref) instead and the surface links to the owner. STARTED BY, START TIME and STATUS bind directly (authority · timestamp · status + counts). DURATION is COMPUTED from timestamp and finished_at and is labelled as computed on every row, because a derived number presented as a recorded one is still a fabrication.
records.steps_are_not_jobs_ruling: The reference's status roll-up reads 'N of M jobs succeeded'. On the estate the sub-unit of a build is a STEP (counts.done / failed / pending / running / stopped over step_results), and `job` is a LIVE estate noun on a different plane (/v1/jobs, runtime job records with a jobType, a checklist and an artifactNames list). Relabelling a step as a job would invent a hierarchy the estate does not have, so every roll-up on this surface says 'steps, not jobs' in its own words and a gate fails if the word 'jobs' is used for a step count.

estate_plane.build_lane: LIVE — the work ledger's `run` entries, rendered with the estate's OWN column names (Build · Started by · Start time · Duration · Status · Proof). Every field is read off the record; a field the record does not carry is a typed dash, never a blank and never an invented value. Cap 50, NAMED whenever it truncates.
estate_plane.proof_anchor: LIVE but PARTIAL, and said so: the state_root is present on the ledger entries the transcript plane recorded and EMPTY on the others. Those rows carry a typed dash whose reason says the proof anchor is genuinely absent — not withheld, and not zero.
estate_plane.task_tray_and_segmented_control: COUNTED, not refused — and this is the deliberate contrast with REG-1. The registry leg refused to print 0 because its plane REFUSED the read; here the plane ANSWERED, so 0 running and 0 failed steps are MEASUREMENTS and they print, each chip naming exactly what was counted. The All/Running/Finished control renders as a live census of the plane and says on-surface that it is a count and not a filter, because this is a read-only projection.
estate_plane.filters: ABSENT — the whole left Search-by/Filter-by panel is typed absences, each reason written for ITS control and all distinct. The load-bearing ones: no estate plane indexes builds by resource or by object type; a 'my builds' toggle would partition a domain of one AND would silently hide the entries whose principal cannot be resolved; the BRANCH radio has no build-record field behind it at all — the estate records a branch only on the workruns plane, which records no status, no start time and no duration and is therefore not an execution plane; the job-type filter would let the reference's vocabulary stand in for the estate's, because jobType lives on /v1/jobs and ledger runs carry a trigger_kind instead; and the date ranges have no server-side range parameter, no recorded tenant timezone, and would quietly exclude every unfinished build.
estate_plane.sessions: REFUSED at port time — /v1/hypervisor/sessions answered HTTP 503 session_registry_unavailable (a pre-existing recorded legacy-slot refusal). No session count is printed and no build is bound to a session: rendering '0 sessions' would convert a closed door into a measurement, and the builds would silently look session-less rather than unresolved.
estate_plane.vendor_global_rail: NOT PORTED — railless per the owner ruling 2026-08-20; nine of the reference's 14 controls are the vendor global rail and are never re-minted on a ported landing.

records.reason: the landing grammar is portable AND the estate has a real build plane to carry it — but only one of its three projections is complete, so the leg's work was choosing the plane and PROVING the choice on-surface. Sixteen planes probed live and classified into four states; the three counts that justify the plane choice re-derived on every render; the build rows rendered verbatim from the work-ledger run lane with a typed dash wherever the record carries nothing; the reference's Outputs and Actions columns answered as REFUSALS rather than filled with different truth; a STEP never relabelled a job; the 3174-transcript plane linked to the Monocle Build timeline rather than re-rendered; every filter control a typed absence with a reason written for it; and every build VERB left on Automations. The landing designation for the jobs seed moves TERMINAL → NOW; the /__ioi/missions substrate keeps its class and its content and stays bound on the seed row.
